content.value_statement: Payment systems must reduce exposure to cardholder data and meet PCI DSS controls. This skill guides secure design, review, and remediation steps.
actual_capabilities: Explains the 12 core PCI DSS requirement areas in practical terms.
Identifies prohibited payment data such as CVV, PIN, and track data.
Provides examples for tokenization, encryption, access control, and audit logging.
Compares common SAQ types for different payment integration models.
Lists common PCI violations and ways to reduce compliance scope.
limitations: It does not replace a Qualified Security Assessor or formal PCI assessment.
It provides illustrative examples that require production review and testing.
It does not verify the current PCI DSS version or card brand rules.
Referenced resources and scripts are not included in the scanned file tree.

use_cases.title: Review Payment Architecture
use_cases.description: Map where cardholder data enters, moves, and is stored before choosing controls.

use_cases.title: Reduce PCI Scope
use_cases.description: Plan hosted payment pages, tokenization, and segmentation to limit systems in scope.

use_cases.title: Prepare Control Evidence
use_cases.description: Create a checklist for encryption, access control, logging, and policy evidence.

prompt_templates.title: Classify My Payment Flow
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review of a payment design.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this payment flow and identify which systems touch cardholder data. Recommend ways to reduce PCI scope.

prompt_templates.title: Check Stored Data
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate review of database fields and logs.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review these payment fields and logs for PCI DSS data storage risks. Flag prohibited data and suggest safe replacements.

prompt_templates.title: Design Secure Controls
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a PCI DSS control plan for tokenization, encryption, access control, audit logging, and vulnerability management.

prompt_templates.title: Assess Readiness Evidence
prompt_templates.prompt: Evaluate this PCI evidence package for gaps against the 12 requirement areas. Prioritize remediation by risk and effort.

output_examples.input: A checkout flow sends card data to our server before creating a processor token.
output: Finding: The server is in PCI scope because it receives card data.
Recommended action: Use a hosted payment page or client-side tokenization.
Evidence to collect: Payment flow diagram, processor integration settings, and server logs without card data.

output_examples.input: A database stores customer ID, payment method token, last four digits, and CVV.
output: Finding: CVV storage is prohibited after authorization.
Recommended action: Remove CVV storage and purge existing records securely.
Evidence to collect: Database schema, purge job results, and logging review.

output_examples.input: The team needs a PCI readiness checklist for a tokenized payment system.
output: Checklist: Confirm no prohibited data storage, enforce TLS, restrict access by role, and review audit logs.
Checklist: Validate encryption key management and maintain vulnerability scanning evidence.
Checklist: Document incident response, security policy, and employee training records.

best_practices: Use hosted payment pages or client-side tokenization when possible.
Encrypt stored PAN and keep encryption keys in managed secret storage.
Document evidence for every control and review logs on a defined schedule.
anti_patterns: Store CVV, PIN, or full track data after authorization.
Hardcode payment processor secrets in source code or examples.
Treat test card examples as proof that a production flow is compliant.

faq.question: Does this skill certify PCI compliance?
faq.answer: No. It supports planning and review, but certification requires the correct PCI process and qualified assessors when required.

faq.question: Can it help choose an SAQ type?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains common SAQ models and highlights architecture facts that influence scope.

faq.question: Does it include production-ready code?
faq.answer: No. The examples are educational and require security review before production use.

faq.question: Can it review logs and database fields?
faq.answer: Yes. It can identify prohibited payment data and suggest safer storage patterns.

faq.question: Does it cover tokenization?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains processor tokens and custom token vault risks at a high level.

faq.question: Which AI tools can use it?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
